key_insight: The paper shows that aqueous solubility can be decomposed into separate chemical and structural contributions by combining an MLP branch for physicochemical descriptors with a GNN branch for molecular graphs only at the final prediction stage.
engineering_relevance: This additive design improves interpretability and robustness for drug-discovery solubility prediction, helping modelers diagnose whether performance comes from global chemistry, molecular topology, or both.
method: Encode physicochemical descriptors with an MLP chemical branch
Encode molecular graph topology with a GNN structural branch
Combine branch outputs additively at prediction time, with optional multiplicative interaction
evidence_signal: Pretraining on AqSolDB and fine-tuning on the smaller BigSolDB2 improved accuracy and reduced run-to-run variability, while maintaining competitive performance across both datasets.
watch_item: The additive decomposition is interpretable, but the optional multiplicative interaction and dataset-specific fine-tuning can complicate attribution and may reduce transferability if training data are biased or limited.
paper_title: An Additive MLP-GNN Framework for Characterizing Chemical and Structural Contributions to Aqueous Solubility
